newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche says to compensate MGAM clients.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche says to compensate MGAM clients.

text.p: Germany's Deutsche Bank AG on Monday said it would have to pay an unspecified level of compensation to investors in its troubled London asset management unit, Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM).

But the bank denied a report in the Guardian newspaper on Saturday that it would have to repatriate 200 million stg to make good investors' losses and that the total cost to Deutsche of sorting out the difficulties would be 400 million stg.
"We have already informed investors that compensation will be paid. This is something that is still being investigated and we have no definitive figure," a bank spokesman told Reuters.

Deutsche has already injected 180 million stg ($303.5 million) into MGAM after an investigation into misvaluations of speculative unlisted stocks led to the temporary suspension of three of its European funds in September.

In an unsourced report on Saturday, the Guardian said that British fund regulator, the Investment Management Regulatory Authority (IMRO), planned to fine Deutsche's London-based investment bank Deutsche Morgan Grenfell more than one million stg and force it to repay up to 200 million stg to investors.
Deutsche's spokesman said IMRO's investigations into the MGAM saga were not yet completed so that any mention of specific levels of compensation was "pure speculation."
"The size of the compensation will be determined on the basis of IMRO's objective calculations," he said, declining to project how high that compensation might be.
He added that it was not clear when IMRO's investigations would be completed.
"That is something for IMRO to say, not us," he said.
Last month, Deutsche announced plans to take over control of MGAM's unit trust business from Frankfurt, thus keeping a closer eye on its operations.
--Catherine O'Mahony, Frankfurt Newsroom, +49 69 756525 ($ = 0.593 British Pounds Sterling)
